subject: Post-call: hyperscaler comparison & private deployment feasibility
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@aperture.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: hyperscaler comparison & private deployment feasibility

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan.

Highlights from the call
- Primary objective: evaluate whether Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem options) meets Aperture's requirements for an air-gapped or tightly controlled deployment while keeping inference costs predictable.
- Main concerns: control-plane connectivity (we discussed private peering vs public control plane), on-prem air-gap feasibility for model hosting, and how unit economics compare to hyperscaler-managed endpoints.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + customer audit readiness were called out; Priya will lead the evidence checklist.

Proposed next tests (low-lift, measurable)
1) Network handshake test (staging VPC): perform control-plane handshake and traceroute from Aperture staging to our control-plane endpoint. Owner: Soojin. ETA: Nov 28–Dec 2.
2) Air-gap smoke test (on-prem): a 1-node offline deployment with a small quantized model (Llama-2/3 7B q4) to validate KV cache persistence, model load times, and restricted TLS cert handling. Owner: Redwood infra + Aperture infra lead. ETA: week of Dec 5.
3) Bench: end-to-end 95th/median latency and tokens-per-second using your 256-token median prompt distribution using a Redwood private instance vs your current hyperscaler endpoint. Owner: Ben (redwood). ETA: preliminary numbers within 3 business days after handshake test.

Immediate asks / action items
- Jordan / Priya: share your staging VPC CIDR block and a preferred contact for networking (name + egress diagram).
- Priya: SOC 2 evidence list we should expect to exchange (we can provide our SOC 2 report + control descriptions).
- Ben: provide ballpark pricing for (a) Dedicated reserved pool, (b) Private with on-prem OE-connector, and (c) Hosted-in-Region API — rough order of magnitude only.

Attachments: proposed-test-matrix.xlsx (test matrix + success criteria), network-topology-drawio.png (sketch we drew on the call).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the handshake test (Nov 28–Dec 2 window). Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Looping in some quick pricing and technical notes for the thread — these are ballparks intended for qualification only. See attached pricing-ballpark.csv for line items.

Pricing (rough)
- Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit): ~ $18k–$32k / GPU-month depending on model family and quantization. Targeting predictability for production SLA.
- Private (VPC connector / on-prem agent): one-time integration + incremental infra ops: ~ $50k engineering uplift + $8k–$20k / mo ops depending on control plane features and support tier.
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): unit costs ~ 30–45% higher than a reserved pool at scale for inference tokens, but no infra ops.

Control plane options (important for jordan’s ask)
- Fully-managed control plane (default hosted): requires outbound TLS to our control-plane endpoints for routing, telemetry, and model pull. Can be set up via private peering in some regions — requires network ACLs and a peering agreement.
- Proxy-only model: we can support a model where control-plane traffic is relayed through a customer-managed proxy inside their VPC; only pre-approved egress endpoints are used. This is our recommended path for customers with stricter networking policies.
- Air-gapped on-prem: possible for inference-only flows if customers accept a manual model distribution process and scheduled syncs for new model artifacts. Hard blockers: automated telemetry and live rollouts (can be replaced with manual processes), and any feature requiring live telemetry-backed rollbacks.

I'll prioritize a compact pricing sheet for the 3 scenarios and highlight trade-offs (latency, ops burden, SLA).

Ben

Jordan — thank you for the quick reply and the constraints. Short answers inline below, and then a suggested schedule.

> One key ask is to understand whether Redwood's control plane requires outbound internet egress or if private peering to your control plane is an option.

Short answer: both are possible. Default is outbound TLS to our hosted control plane. Private peering is supported in US regions with a peering setup (requires IP allow-listing and shared peering config). If you need zero outbound internet, our proxy-only or fully air-gapped model distribution pattern is the fallback (the trade-off is losing automatic rollouts/telemetry).

> Can you call out any hard blockers that would make an air-gapped deployment impossible?

We don't see any absolute blockers for inference-only air-gapped installs. Trade-offs to note:
- No live telemetry for quality/regression alerts (can be done via manual uploads),
- Manual model updates (we provide signed model artifacts and a vetted distribution process),
- Some advanced features like live canary rollouts and streaming debug traces require a reachable control plane.

Suggested schedule (proposed by Redwood)
- Nov 30: handshake test (control-plane traceroute + cert exchange) — 1 hour window.
- Dec 6: air-gap smoke test (on-prem single-node) — 2–3 hour window with infra leads.
- Dec 9–10: benchmark run and delivery of preliminary latency/tps report.

Next steps (I'll do these today)
- Send a calendar invite for Nov 30 to Samir (your infra lead) + our networking engineer.
- Ben will circulate the compact pricing sheet by EOD tomorrow.
- Aisha will prepare a starter SOC 2 evidence checklist and share via Drive.

If that works, we’ll lock Nov 30 10:00–11:00 PT as the handshake slot.

Thanks — appreciate the collaboration.

Best,
Soojin
